message:
Publish the dev-node lane at canonical paths and pin its harness

operator_review reported four times that it could not find devnode/tui or
ops/ci/devnode.sh anywhere in the repository. It was right: the lane existed
only in a scratch tree on the development host, so nobody could review the
thing I was citing as proof. This puts every byte of it at a canonical path.

The lane drives `bullet tui` through a real pseudo-terminal and the Portal
through a real browser, both against an authenticated daemon. That session and
the provider credentials behind it exist on one machine, so the lane refuses to
run anywhere else, twice over: ops/ci/devnode.sh refuses under GITHUB_ACTIONS,
and ops/ci/workflow-policy.sh refuses any hosted workflow that so much as names
it. The second guard is the one a maintainer trips over first, so it is the one
with hostile fixtures: a job that runs the lane, a commented-out mention, a
matrix entry, and a symlinked workflow entry.

Manifest classification, per the review. My first attempt pruned ./devnode from
the build-subject search. Both reviewers rejected that and they were right:
pruning would have made every future manifest under that directory invisible to
the guard, which is the opposite of what the guard is for. Instead there are now
two pinned classes. Product manifests are what ships. Proof manifests belong to
harnesses that are never a product dependency and are built by no lane other
than the one they prove; crates/bullet-wire/fuzz/Cargo.toml set that precedent
and devnode/tui/Cargo.toml joins it. Both the manifest and its lock are
digest-pinned exactly as a product manifest is, and four new canary cases cover
what pruning would have let through: a second harness beside the pinned one, a
missing harness, a changed harness dependency, and a changed lock.

The four product manifest pins and the seven existing subject pins are
byte-identical to main.

Proved on the development host before pushing: the lint lane passes end to end,
the build-subject canary passes and fails on a falsified pin, and the workflow
policy passes and fails when the devnode guard is neutered.

Register the devnode lane in the proof-lane registry

The hosted fast lane caught what my local lint lane could not: assurance_controls
control_manifests_route_to_real_local_proof parses every non-empty line between
`case "$lane" in` and `*)` in scripts/ci-local.sh as a dispatcher row, so the two
comment lines I put beside the new case arm were read as malformed rows. The note
now sits above the case statement, where it is still next to the thing it
explains and is not mistaken for a row.

With that fixed the same test reported the real omission: a new lane must be
declared in agent/proof-lanes.toml and in the expected registry, or the
dispatcher and the registry disagree. Both now carry devnode, with
requires_network true, because the lane fetches the pinned Tuiwright revision and
talks to a daemon.

That test is the control that stops a lane from existing in the dispatcher while
being invisible to the register, which is a near relative of the finding this
whole branch closes.

Give the harness its own workspace root, or it cannot build at all

Found by running the lane against the live authenticated daemon rather than by
reading it. devnode/tui/Cargo.toml said it was "excluded from the Hub workspace"
and nothing excluded it, so cargo read ../../Cargo.toml and refused:

    error: current package believes it is in a workspace when it is not
    current:   devnode/tui/Cargo.toml
    workspace: Cargo.toml

An empty [workspace] table in the harness manifest makes it its own root. Doing
it there rather than through an `exclude` in the Hub manifest keeps every product
manifest byte-identical, which is the promise the proof-only class rests on. The
proof-only pin is regenerated for the new bytes.

This is exactly the failure the hosted graph cannot catch, because the lane
refuses to run hosted by design. It was caught the only way it could be: by
running the lane. All eight console flows then pass against a real authenticated
session on this host, serially, in 7.31 seconds.

Record the console at 1920x1080, with its own frame masters

Every media artifact in this repository misses the geometry it declares. The two
terminal GIFs are 2049x1323 and 1903x1228, the second of those despite being
named "1080", and the Portal capture is 1920x1200. The bullet.real-media.v1
manifest declares 1920x1080 and nothing has ever produced it.

The arithmetic was never hard, it was simply never done. Tuiwright renders a
screen as cols*cell_width by rows*cell_height and draws real JetBrains Mono
scaled to the cell height, so a larger cell means larger glyphs rather than gaps.
120 columns by 36 rows at a 16x30 cell with no padding is exactly 1920x1080, and
120x36 is a terminal size a person would actually use.

Run against the live console on this host, just now:

    DEVNODE_RECORD_COMPLETE: tui-1080p.gif at 1920x1080, 9 frames, 9 masters

Frames come from the pseudo-terminal own parsed screen model, so they are native
frames rather than a re-render of an asciicast. Every frame is also written as a
lossless 1920x1080 PNG, because the M1 gate asks for original masters and
media/dogfood/README.md states plainly that the current packet has none. The
recorder reads the geometry back out of the encoded file own header and refuses
DEVNODE_RECORD_GIF_GEOMETRY_DRIFT rather than trusting the encoder, which is the
check every existing artifact would have failed.

Two properties worth naming because they are the reason to trust the output. It
records nothing it has not first asserted, so the artifact cannot contain a frame
the harness did not verify. And run.json names the beats it did NOT record and
why: today that is every beat needing durable work, because the ledger holds
none, and inventing rows would make the recording a mock.

The lane builds it and does not run it. A recording is a deliberate act against a
real session with a private output directory; a lane that published media as a
side effect would be publishing without anyone asking.

The proof-only manifest class now holds two entries, which is what it was built
for. Product manifest pins and the seven subject pins remain byte-identical to
main, and the canary covers the second harness exactly as it covers the first.
